transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. What brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in because I’m just tired all the time. By midmorning at work—I'm a claims adjuster—after just reviewing some files or walking a junior adjuster through a claim, it already feels like my body and my brain are just running on empty.
How long have you been experiencing this persistent level of exhaustion?

It’s been quite a while now. I’d say... probably about three years and three months. It started right around the time I was moved into a higher-responsibility role at the company. That was when I had to start mentoring the newer adjusters and overseeing our new workflow systems. So, yeah, it's been going on ever since then.
When you experience this exhaustion, do you find that your symptoms significantly worsen after physical or mental exertion, and does it take more than 24 hours for you to recover from that?

No, not really. I mean, I'm just always tired. It doesn't seem to matter if I've had a really busy day with complex claims or a quiet day just catching up on emails. The exhaustion is just... always there. It doesn't get worse after doing something specific, and it's not like I have a crash and then recover. I just never really feel rested to begin with.
During these past three years, have you had any periods lasting two months or longer where you felt completely like your usual self and free of this constant exhaustion?
No, I haven't. There hasn't been any break like that. It's just been a steady, everyday thing for the whole three years. I haven't had a single month, let alone two, where I felt normal or rested.
Over the past three years, have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite, such as eating much more or much less than you normally would?

No, not really. My appetite hasn't changed much at all. I eat about the same amount I always have. I just don't have the energy to cook anything complicated, but I'm definitely not eating way more or way less than usual.
During these past three years, have you felt down, sad, or hopeless most of the day, more days than not?

Yes, I have. Most days, it just feels like there's this gray film over everything. Even when my husband is being really kind, or we're cooking together with the family... I just kind of go through the motions. I participate, but I don't really feel the enjoyment I used to.
Over these past three years, have you struggled with your sleep, such as having trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping too much?

No, my sleep has been pretty normal. I don't have any trouble falling asleep or staying asleep, and I wouldn't say I'm sleeping too much, either. I just wake up feeling tired, but the actual sleeping part is fine.
Do you often feel down on yourself, or do you frequently feel like you are inadequate or a failure?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I don't feel like a failure or anything. I know I do my job well as a claims adjuster, and I'm a good wife and mother. I don't really get down on myself in that way. It's more just... that overall feeling of being down, like I mentioned, rather than feeling inadequate.
Do you find that you have difficulty concentrating on tasks or making decisions in your daily life?

No, not really. I can concentrate fine at work—reviewing claims takes a lot of focus, and I don't have any issues getting through it. And making decisions hasn't been a problem either, whether it's at work or just figuring out things at home.
Have you noticed that you have lost interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, such as your hobbies or social interactions?

No, not really. I still enjoy the things I've always liked doing. I still like spending time with my family and I still enjoy my hobbies. It's not that I don't care about those things anymore, it's just that I have this constant feeling of being low while I'm doing them. But the interest is definitely still there.
Do you often find yourself feeling hopeless about the future?

Yes, I do. I just... I keep thinking this is what the rest of my working life is going to be like. Just more audits, more new systems to learn, more pressure. It's hard to look ahead and... I just can't really picture things feeling lighter again.
When you are feeling that 'gray film' over things, do you find it harder than usual to make up your mind about things or to keep your thoughts focused?

No, I really don't. Like I mentioned before, my focus is fine. Even when I'm feeling that low way, I can still get through my work and review the claims without any trouble. And making decisions isn't any harder than it usually is. It's just my mood that's affected, not my ability to think clearly or decide things.
